items.t: September exports set a monthly record and nine-month export earnings reach a new high
items.sum: Export earnings for the first nine months of the year are the highest on record.

items.t: Exports pass US$ 13.6 bn in January to September, up about 5%
items.sum: Goods and services both contributed to the year-on-year growth.

items.t: Bank of Ceylon plans a listed debt issue of up to Rs. 30 bn, the largest the country has seen
items.sum: The state bank is going to the market for long-term funding through a listed instrument.

items.t: Debt office rejects every bid at its domestic dollar bond auction
items.sum: Market sources said the rates bidders asked for were too high.

items.t: Laugfs Gas explores selling a stake in its Hambantota LPG terminal
items.sum: Early, informal talks with potential buyers are under way.

items.t: Corrugated carton makers face growing cost pressure
items.sum: Rising input costs are squeezing margins in the packaging sector.

items.t: Sampath Bank's Rs. 10 bn debenture issue is oversubscribed by 22.7%
items.sum: Applications of about Rs. 12.27 bn came in for the Rs. 10 bn maximum.

items.t: Colombo shares fall 2.48% over the week, a fifth straight losing session
items.sum: The ASPI ended the week lower after consecutive declines.

items.t: Tourist arrivals up about 5% in the first 22 days of October
items.sum: Around 119,800 visitors arrived, compared with the same period last year.

items.t: Government plans 18 industrial zones to draw investment
items.sum: The zones are meant to expand manufacturing capacity and growth.

items.t: Fitch gives Asia Asset Finance's proposed senior debt an expected A+(lka) rating
items.sum: The rating is expected, pending completion of the issue.

items.t: Vallibel One buys about 31% of The Fortress Resorts for roughly Rs. 730 mn
items.sum: The shares came from two related parties.

items.t: IMF projects Sri Lanka will raise US$ 3 bn in global bond markets by 2028
items.sum: A return to international borrowing is part of the IMF's outlook.

items.t: Cabinet backs mandatory national standards for imported car and three-wheeler tyres
items.sum: Imported tyres would have to meet Sri Lanka Standards.

items.t: Government tightens tyre import rules to protect local manufacturers
items.sum: Quality compliance checks on imported motor vehicle tyres are being enforced.

items.t: Fitch gives CBC Finance's proposed subordinated debt an expected BBB+(lka) rating
items.sum: The rating is expected, pending completion of the issue.

items.t: Hambantota port operator sees new openings as container ships return to the Suez route
items.sum: HIPG expects more business as the shipping route recovers.

items.t: IPS commentary on policy priorities for durable growth after the recovery
items.sum: A Talking Economics piece on what comes after stabilisation.

items.t: Sri Lanka's terrorism law could put a trade lifeline at risk
items.sum: An analysis of how the legislation may affect trade access.

items.t: Government moves to pass a public-private partnership bill
items.sum: The bill aims to bring private investment into infrastructure.

items.t: Four-hour daily power cuts proposed, pending regulator approval
items.sum: The system operator has asked the utilities commission to approve the cuts.

items.t: China Merchants Port, Access Engineering and the Ports Authority drop a logistics hub plan
items.sum: The three parties have abandoned the South Asia logistics hub project.

items.t: Global securities regulators meet in Colombo on enforcement and cooperation
items.sum: The Securities and Exchange Commission hosted the IOSCO discussions.

items.t: President says ports and the power grid will open to private investors
items.sum: The government plans to bring private capital into both sectors.

items.t: IPS holds roundtables on its State of the Economy 2026 report
items.sum: Discussions on the institute's annual economic assessment.

items.t: Economy.lk review of Sri Lanka's return to upper-middle-income status
items.sum: Looks at progress, remaining challenges and the path ahead.

items.t: US trade chief works to win public support for tariffs, which polls show are unpopular
items.sum: Bloomberg homepage listing. The US is Sri Lanka's largest market for apparel.

items.t: Nuclear inspectors see no evidence that Iran has repaired the sites bombed by the US
items.sum: Bloomberg homepage listing. Middle East tension feeds into oil prices.

items.t: Bloomberg's ticker shows crude near US$ 100 a barrel and the US 10-year yield near 5%
items.sum: Market data on the Bloomberg homepage when checked on 28 Oct, not a headline.
